content.text:
I implemented `phase`, `phase_filter` and `option`, plus `check`, `inspect_entries`, a `load` reader for the four sections, and helpers for creating and copying elements. Of 509 comparison cases plus about 1,300 random sessions (some opened from projects with walls, doors, views and option sets), the only 8 that differ use `graphics`, `template`, `section` or `filter`, which are still stubs. The same scenarios built as projects by the original and opened in both programs match. Nothing was committed and the worktree is untouched.

**The file:** `/tmp/styles-agent/phasing/repo/src/styles/phasing.rs`. It keeps the entry points `run`, `check` and `inspect_entries(s, out)` and uses only `common.rs`.

**`phase`** — matches the original on:
- the listing reply and every error, in the original's order of checks;
- the undo step: edits make one even when nothing changes, `now` alone never does;
- the saved file: `phases` is written only when it isn't Existing/New Construction, and library entries are added, renamed or removed;
- `before`/`after`, including pinning: putting a phase first, or deleting the first, gives every phased element without a value the old first phase's GUID. Doors and windows aren't pinned; they follow their wall.
- `delete` with `into`: every reference to the deleted phase moves to `into`, and a demolition that ends up before its element was made is pulled up to the made phase, doors counting their wall's. Without `into`, view-filter and schedule rules that named it fall back to its name as text.
- `now`, and `overrides` merging with serde's error texts.

**`phase_filter`** — create, change, show and delete match, including the "is the phase filter of {view}/view template `T`" refusals (views by id first, then templates). `phase_filters` is written only when it differs from the English defaults.

**`option`** — matches the original's order of checks (all parameters read first, then the name rules), the four reply shapes, renames of sets and options (library, rules and `now` follow), and replacing options (new ones added before old ones go, primary kept or the first; an option holding elements is refused). `accept` and `delete` remove dependants and return the `deleted` list. The undo step follows options, primary, rename, delete or accept, but not show or `now`.

**What doesn't match, or is approximate:**
- `check` runs phase rules and project-parameter rules separately, but the original goes through each element's params once, in sorted order. An element with both a bad project parameter and a bad phase value names a different one first. `check_with(pr, hook)` takes the parameters rule as a callback to fix this.
- The dependants deleted with an option set are what I observed: doors and windows of deleted walls, anything whose `host` is gone (tags, railings, spot elevations), and dimensions left with fewer than two references (the others just lose the reference). The core should own one shared delete routine.

**Shared-file edits needed** (all four are in `/tmp/styles-agent/phasing/core.patch`):
- `project.rs`: in `TOP_ORDER`, `standard` moves to right after `option_sets`. The observed order is `… parameters, view_filters, view_templates, phases, phase_filters, phase_overrides, option_sets, standard, object_styles, line_patterns …`.
- `session.rs`: `execute` must save `now_phase`/`now_option` and put them back when a command fails or the check refuses it, as the original does.
- `basic.rs`: `new` and `open` reset `now_phase`/`now_option`. `open` should call `styles::phasing::load` (its error goes after "{path} is not a BIMCraft project: ", and its paths go into the reply's `left_out`/`left_out_count`), then run `check::check` with errors as "{path}: {msg}". The original runs the model check on open: "open: x.bimcraft: wall 100002: it can't be demolished…".
- `inspect.rs`: merge `styles::inspect_entries(s)`, which gives `phases`, `phase_filters`, `phase_overrides` (patterns by name) and `option_sets` (primary by name). `inspect` doesn't show `now`.

**What the other commands must provide:**
- Phases, filters, sets and options are referenced by library GUID everywhere: element params `Phase Created`/`Phase Demolished`/`Design Option`, view and template `graphics` (`phase`, `phase_filter`, `options` as {set: option}), filter and schedule rule values, and override fill patterns. `modify`, `graphics`, `template`, `filter` and `schedule` must store GUIDs and show names. With that, renames need no element updates.
- A name that doesn't resolve can be stored raw; `check` then gives the original's error, e.g. "level 100000: there's no phase `Nope`…".
- `graphics`/`template` can call `check_view_graphics` and prefix their command name to get the original's texts.
- New elements: call `stamp_new(pr, now_phase, now_option, &mut e)`. It sets `Phase Created` unless the session's phase is the first (doors and windows are named anyway) and sets `Design Option`.
- Copies: call `stamp_copy`. When the session has a phase, the copy takes it and drops `Phase Demolished`; when it has an option, the copy takes it; otherwise the copy keeps its own.
- `set_param` puts `params` where each category's struct has it (before `base_offset` on rooms, before `room_bounding` on columns, otherwise last) and keeps its keys sorted.
